title: VENTILATED THERMOWOOD® FAÇADE SYSTEM
subtitle: VENTILATED TIMBER CLADDING WITH PIR INSULATION
metaTitle: Ventilated ThermoWood® Façade System | EcoViva Mallorca
metaDescription: Technical guidance for a ventilated ThermoWood® timber façade with PIR insulation, durable substructure and moisture-managed cavity construction in Mallorca.
heroAlt: Ventilated timber façade build-up with five numbered callouts identifying the structural wall, PIR façade insulation, timber battens, ventilated cavity and ThermoWood® cladding.
cleanHeroAlt: Clean ventilated timber façade build-up with masonry wall, PIR insulation, timber battens and ThermoWood® cladding.
overview: The ventilated ThermoWood® façade combines high-performance external insulation with a ventilated timber substructure and durable thermally modified wood cladding. The open cavity supports airflow, helps drain incidental moisture and protects the external wall while creating a warm architectural finish for Mallorca's climate.
overviewNote: Final design must be verified for the substrate, façade height, wind exposure, fire requirements, ventilation openings, fixing method and project-specific conditions.
why: One point of contact from concept to completion
layers: Prepared masonry or concrete wall supporting the complete façade system.
High-performance rigid insulation reducing heat transfer through the external wall.
Durable timber substructure creating the ventilated cavity and supporting the cladding.
Continuous drainage and airflow space behind the external timber finish.
Thermally modified timber finish providing stability and natural architectural character.
principles: Keep the base-to-top cavity open for continuous airflow and drainage.
Use a suitable vapour-open breather membrane and correctly detailed openings.
Select exterior-grade battens and corrosion-resistant fixings for façade loads and coastal exposure.
Allow for timber movement; coordinate openings, corners, interfaces, base and top closures.
components: Substructure forming the ventilation and drainage cavity.
Protects cavity openings while maintaining airflow.
designOptions: Modern vertical rhythm with dark joints.
Varied board widths for a dynamic façade.
Narrow ribs creating depth and shadow.
Natural ageing to a soft grey patina.
ageingNote: Untreated ThermoWood® naturally develops a silver-grey surface. Appearance varies with exposure, detailing and maintenance.
requirements: Use compatible façade components selected for the substrate, insulation, cavity depth, cladding profile, fixing method, façade height, wind exposure and coastal environment. Ventilation openings, insect protection, drainage, fire performance, movement joints and all interfaces must be project-verified. Final design and execution must comply with the CTE, applicable product documentation and project-specific requirements.
